concept.title: Showing pages inside another page
concept.shortdesc: If you show the publication's pages inside a frame on a page of your own, such as a presentation screen or a guided tour, the embedded view shows each page's content without its masthead, contents, pagination or footer.

conbody.p: embedded viewiframegovuk.embedSome publishers place their own pages inside another page they control: a kiosk, a guided tour, a lecture theatre that shows a page on its projection screen. There the page's furniture works against the reader, and a link that leaves the frame replaces the page around it. Build with -Dgovuk.embed=yes, frame a page with ?embed=1 after its address, and the page shows its content only.
conbody.codeblock: <iframe title="Installing the plugin, from the manual" src="/manual/topics/install.html?embed=1"></iframe>

section.title: What changes, and what does not

ul.li: The masthead, phase banner, contents, previous and next links and footer are hidden, and the content takes the width they used.
A link to another page of the same site keeps embed=1, so the reader stays in the embedded view inside the frame. A link opened in a new tab, and a link to another site, behave as usual.

Links in diagrams that are drawn into the page lose a target of _top or _parent. Diagrams made to be shown as an <object> often carry one so that a click leaves the object; drawn into the page, it would replace the page around the frame. A diagram shown with DITA's <object> element keeps its own links.
The view applies only inside a frame. The same address opened in a browser window, or with JavaScript turned off, shows the full page, so a copied link never leads to a page with no way on.
Without the parameter nothing changes: no page loads the script.

section.p: The view does not exist with govuk.branding=official or nhs: those identities' header and footer belong on every page. The build ignores the parameter and says so (GOVK014W).

section.title: What the framing page must do

ul.li: Give the iframe a title that says what it holds; it is the frame's name for screen readers.

Allow the framing. The headers in include frame-ancestors 'none', which forbids any framing. A host that frames its own pages sets frame-ancestors 'self', or names the framing site, in its place. A <meta> policy cannot set this; it has to be a header.

section.title: Styling the embedded view
section.p: In the embedded view the page's html element has the class app-embed. Your own stylesheet () can use it, for example to set larger type for a screen read from across a room, or to hide links that would lead back to the framing page:
